headline: NTPC Green Energy seeks bidders for the balance of system of a 250 MW / 1,000 MWh battery storage project at Kayamkulam, Kerala; NTPC supplies the battery containers, BMS and grid-forming inverters itself, and bids close on 11 Dec
so: A 1 GWh grid-forming storage build in Kerala with batteries bought separately by NTPC: another large cell and container order to come in India.
short: NTPC Green tenders works for a 1 GWh battery project in Kerala

headline: China awarded 53.6 GWh of energy storage in October, 7% less than in September, mostly EPC contracts; the average 4-hour system award rose 17% to about $81.9/kWh while 2-hour systems slipped 2%
so: Chinese 4-hour system award prices jumped in October: the long fall in storage system prices may be bottoming out.

headline: InfoLink weekly: lithium carbonate stays near its lows at about $13,280 a tonne; the 314 Ah storage cell slips to $46.0/kWh as cheaper materials sharpen price competition, while system prices hold
so: Storage cell prices edge down again with lithium flat: cell buyers keep a slight price advantage this week.

headline: Lithium futures recover 2.1% on 11 Nov to about $13,270 a tonne as traders cut positions, while the SMM spot price keeps slipping to about $13,500 on thin, need-only buying
so: Lithium bounces within a low range: no change yet to the low raw-material cost of LFP cells.

headline: A Chinese lithium giant says lithium price swings have become more extreme (headline only, not verified)
so: A large producer flags sharper lithium price swings: cell costs could move faster than usual in both directions.

headline: Geely chairman Li Shufu warns that EV batteries wearing out before the cars could become a big problem in China, as full pack replacement is too costly; Geely backs battery swapping by taking a 30% stake in Nio Power
so: A major carmaker says sealed packs that outlive their cells hurt EV resale values: a push for repairable packs and swapping.

headline: BMW will use LFP cells in base versions of some Neue Klasse models, starting with the China-only iX3 long-wheelbase, alongside its cell-to-pack 800 V NMC packs with 46 mm round cells
so: A premium carmaker adds LFP to entry versions of its new EVs: LFP keeps winning share in car packs.

headline: BYD is reported to be considering a battery factory on the former Galp refinery site at Matosinhos, Portugal; no size, investment or timing given and BYD has not commented
so: A possible new BYD battery plant in Europe: more Chinese cell capacity close to European carmakers.

headline: China's October NEV retail sales fall 13.7% on a year to 1.109 million (CPCA), but NEVs reach a record 67.5% of car sales as the overall market drops 27%; BYD leads with a 22.4% share, then Geely 11.8% and Leapmotor 7.5%
so: China's car market shrinks while EV share hits a record: slower domestic EV battery demand, adding to spare cell capacity.

headline: Ravindra Energy plans to sell its solar plants to fund its electric heavy-truck unit Energy in Motion (EIM), whose quarterly sales rose to ₹130.8 crore from ₹44 crore; EIM runs at about 2,000 trucks a year and plans to grow its charging and swap stations from 8 to 15 by December and 40 by March 2027
so: An Indian e-truck maker raises money for growth and a corridor swap network: more competition and charging cover for heavy e-trucks.

headline: Tinci Materials signs a long-term deal to supply EVE Energy with about 450,000 t of electrolyte (±20%) in 2027–2029, prices set by later orders; CATL also signs a strategic cooperation agreement with aluminium group Chinalco
so: A top cell maker locks in electrolyte for three years: big buyers securing materials ahead of a strong storage cell build-out.

headline: Bus fleets in Benxi, Changzhou, Guiyang and Lanzhou sign deals with CATL on the same day for replacement batteries, aftermarket service, city battery-swap networks, recycling and V2G, as China's 2015–2018 electric buses reach their battery replacement window
so: China's first big e-bus fleets now need new packs: battery replacement and swapping become a business of their own for bus operators.

headline: CATL chairman Robin Zeng says its battery-swap network, aiming for more than 3,000 car swap stations in China by end-2026, will speed up sodium-ion adoption by covering longer trips; CATL expects 10,000–20,000 cars on its Naxtra sodium-ion cells (up to 175 Wh/kg) this year
so: Sodium-ion paired with swapping to cover its range gap: a route for sodium cells into cars that limits lithium price exposure.

headline: Lithium carbonate futures close at about $13,000 a tonne on 10 Nov, close to their 4 Nov low and almost 60% below the mid-May peak; Fubao puts battery-grade spot at about $13,630, and analysts see a possible floor in Nov–Dec as prices dip below some mining and recycling costs
so: Lithium stuck near its 2026 low: cell material costs stay at the bottom of the range for current quotes.

headline: China extends its pause on export controls for lithium batteries, LFP cathode and artificial graphite anode (2025 Announcement No. 58) and five related notices from 11 Nov 2026 to 10 Jan 2027, in step with the US–China trade truce
so: Cell, cathode and graphite imports from China stay licence-free for two more months, but the risk returns on 10 Jan 2027.
short: China extends battery and graphite export-control pause to 10 Jan 2027

headline: Olectra plans a new generation of more localised electric buses for India and export in January–March 2027; its order book tops 8,000 buses, and it delivered 401 vehicles in July–September (+7%) with revenue up 5% to ₹687 crore
so: India's largest e-bus order book gets a new model range by early 2027: more competition and battery demand in Indian e-buses.
short: Olectra to launch new-generation e-buses by March 2027

headline: Lithium's rebound fades: the Guangzhou lc2701 contract falls 4.85% on 9 Nov to about $13,060 a tonne, as November cell output plans slip and a restart of the Jiaxiawo mine looks closer; exchange warehouse receipts rose to 23,700 lots
so: Lithium falls back toward its lows: cell and cathode costs keep easing, with a mine restart the next test.

headline: BMW adds Samsung SDI (Europe) and LG Energy Solution (North America) as suppliers of its sixth-generation cylindrical cells from near the end of the decade, alongside CATL and EVE, and is building five pack assembly plants near its car plants
so: A big carmaker spreads cell orders across Chinese and Korean makers and local plants: more regional sourcing in EV cells.

headline: Interview: a Turin Polytechnic battery professor says commercial sodium-ion cells reach about 175 Wh/kg against about 205 Wh/kg for advanced LFP and keep over 95% capacity after 5,000 cycles, narrowing the gap for stationary storage
so: Sodium-ion is closing on LFP for grid storage, though output is still under 1% of lithium-ion and no cost figure is given.

headline: Portugal opens its first grid-connection auctions since 2021 for up to 1,050 MVA: 750 MVA for standalone batteries and 300 MVA for renewables with storage, both needing at least four hours; applications close 22 Dec
so: Another European market asks for four-hour batteries: more global demand for long-duration storage systems.

headline: Lithium rebounds for a second day on 6 Nov: the Guangzhou lc2701 contract closes near $13,820 a tonne and SMM's battery-grade spot average rises about 2% to $13,970, helped by restocking and falling smelter stocks; analysts stay split on whether the bottom is in
so: Lithium steadies after a near-halving since May: cell and cathode costs may stop falling, though views on the bottom still differ.

headline: Wood Mackenzie: sodium-ion cells should reach cost parity with LFP at leading makers by late 2026, with more than 70 GWh already under supply agreements; at module and system level parity is not expected before 2030, and LFP stays the default for 2–4 hour storage
so: Sodium-ion is becoming a real second chemistry at cell level, but LFP keeps its lead in storage systems for several years.

headline: Exide says its 6 GWh lithium-ion cell plant in Bengaluru was commissioned on 23 Sep: LFP cells already earn revenue, a line for 300+ Ah prismatic storage cells is ready, major carmakers should start buying from about February, and it puts its cost gap to imported Chinese cells at 5–10%
so: A second large Indian cell plant is running: local LFP cells for two-wheelers and storage, still a little dearer than Chinese imports.

headline: Hyderabad's TREX Energy commissions an automated battery module assembly line in E-City for 52S packs used in its 261 kWh and 5 MWh storage systems, and plans a second plant in Madhya Pradesh
so: One more Indian BESS assembler adds pack lines: local container capacity keeps growing while cells are still imported.

headline: CATL's chief scientist names lithium-air as a long-term research direction; CarNewsChina notes there is no product timeline and that the reported 2,000 km range is theoretical, with sodium-ion and solid-state cells remaining CATL's nearer priorities
so: Lithium-air is lab research only: no change to cell choices for years.

headline: Gotion shareholders approve three LFP joint ventures with Volkswagen's PowerCo worth about €3.22 billion: 29.1 GWh a year of cells in Valencia (Spain), 8.4 GWh in Šurany (Slovakia) and 100,000 t a year of LFP cathode in Kenitra (Morocco); regulatory clearances and final supply terms are still pending
so: A Chinese cell maker and a carmaker plan 37.5 GWh of LFP cells in Europe: more LFP supply outside China, but not before clearances and construction.

headline: Fluence's CEO Julian Nebreda and CFO Ahmed Pasha step down with immediate effect; board member Axel Meier becomes interim CEO and Ricardo Roizen interim CFO, and a new board committee will oversee manufacturing and customer delivery; contracted backlog is $6.4 billion
so: Top-level exit at a large Western storage integrator focused on fixing manufacturing and delivery: execution records matter when choosing integrators.

headline: Olectra puts 35 nine-metre air-conditioned electric buses with Blade batteries into service in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Maharashtra), run by Evey Trans; it reports more than 4,500 buses deployed in over 55 cities and an order book above 7,950 vehicles
so: Another city fleet from one of India's largest e-bus order books: close to 8,000 more buses still to deliver, each needing a battery pack.

headline: NHPC seeks developers for 800 MW of battery storage at the 1.2 GW Jalaun solar park in Uttar Pradesh, in two options (800 MW / 4.8 GWh or 800 MW / 3.2 GWh) on a build-own-operate basis; bids due mid-December, completion within 18 months
so: Another multi-GWh solar-plus-storage tender in India: 3.2–4.8 GWh more battery demand for delivery around 2028.
short: NHPC tenders 800 MW / up to 4.8 GWh of storage at Jalaun solar park

headline: FADA: India's EV retail sales hit a record of about 3.55 lakh in October, up 44.9% on a year, lifting EV share of all vehicles to about 11.5%; EV share reached 62.6% in three-wheelers, 9.7% in two-wheelers, 7.3% in cars and 4.3% in commercial vehicles, with demand ahead of supply
so: Record Indian EV sales with commercial-vehicle EV share above 4%: rising pack demand across segments, and supply rather than demand is the limit.

headline: Blackbuck EV shows the ELON 3X, a 15-metre three-axle electric sleeper coach with 42 berths and 425 kWh or 565 kWh battery options; reservations are open and commercial production is targeted for mid-2027
so: A 15-metre electric sleeper coach with packs up to 565 kWh: long-distance e-buses in India would need some of the largest packs on the road.
short: Blackbuck EV shows 15 m electric sleeper coach with up to 565 kWh

headline: An International Solar Alliance report on India's energy storage cites CEA projections of 888 GWh of storage needed by 2035-36, of which 321 GWh battery storage, and urges revenue stacking, ancillary-service access, grid-forming inverters in new tenders and a second VGF tranche by 2027
so: 321 GWh of battery storage needed in India by 2035-36: a long runway for BESS demand if market rules let projects earn from several services.

headline: Premier Energies says its 6 GWh BESS Phase I project, with RCT as technology and equity partner, targets commissioning in July 2027, with site and civil work under way; it lists 12 GWh of BESS container capacity under construction
so: A solar maker adds 6 GWh of storage-system capacity in India from mid-2027: more local BESS suppliers ahead of domestic-content rules.

headline: Albemarle's third-quarter energy-storage sales rose 58% to $1.12 billion on a realised lithium price of about $20 per kg, but it expects fourth-quarter sales and margins to fall on lower prices, cuts 2026 capex to $300–350 million and says global lithium demand rose 48% to August
so: The largest Western lithium producer expects lower prices and spends less: near-term lithium stays soft, while capex cuts slow new supply later.

headline: SMM: China battery-grade lithium carbonate spot averaged about $13,690 a tonne on 5 Nov, down 4.6% in a week, while the Guangzhou most-traded contract closed near $13,670, up 3.6% on the week; social inventory fell by about 3,000 t to 125,391 t
so: Lithium spot keeps easing while futures rebound and stocks fall: a soft but stabilising price for LFP cathode and cells.

headline: SMM: bids in a 2026 energy-storage framework procurement by CHN Energy's renewables arm ranged from about $84.5 to $89.3 per kWh (excl. VAT), up from about $68.7 in CNNC's mid-October tender, while mainstream storage cell quotes held near $72.6 per kWh
so: Chinese storage tender prices are rising again: higher BESS equipment costs for buyers ordering for 2027.

headline: India plans to make power distributors buy energy storage with their renewable power purchases; Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal says the rules should be final by March, with the required share still under discussion, and an advisory for developers to add storage will become mandatory
so: A storage purchase mandate for Indian distributors would turn today's tender-by-tender demand into a standing obligation: steadier BESS demand from 2027.
short: India plans to make distributors buy storage with renewables

headline: SNE Research: outside China, CATL's EV battery installations rose 46.7% to 143.7 GWh in January–September (33.7% share) and BYD's 66.8% to 45.9 GWh, while LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI together fell 13.5% to 113 GWh
so: Chinese cell makers keep gaining ground outside China as Korean makers shrink: buyers abroad lean further on Chinese cell supply.

headline: SNE Research: global storage-battery shipments reached 779.9 GWh in January–September, up 73%, with a record 286.8 GWh in the third quarter; CATL leads with 198.3 GWh, ahead of Hithium (75.7 GWh) and EVE (71.6 GWh)
so: Storage-cell demand is still growing fast worldwide, which keeps storage-cell factories busy and limits how far cell prices can fall.

headline: A study released by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (NETRA with ARCI, CSIR-NCL, IIT Madras and Deloitte) finds Indian cathode, anode, electrolyte, separator and foil makers face costs 18–61% above imports, and proposes capital subsidies or operating incentives to close part of the gap
so: Indian-made cell materials cost well above imports today: localising cells depends on new support for component makers.

headline: Tata's Agratas is installing equipment at its Sanand (Gujarat) and Somerset (UK) cell plants, with anchor demand from Tata Motors and JLR; its Bengaluru lab works on LFP for mass-market cars and Oxford on NMC, and assets more than doubled in FY26
so: India's largest planned cell plant is moving towards commissioning: Indian-made LFP cells for EVs come closer, initially for Tata vehicles.

headline: Honda will build its Alpha electric SUV at Tapukara, Rajasthan, with two LFP pack options and a world premiere in India on 2 December, for export to Japan and Southeast Asia; cells are reported to come from CATL's plant in Indonesia
so: Another carmaker makes India an EV export base with LFP packs: more electric-car volume in India, with cells still imported.

headline: Mercedes is developing small converters on each cell or cell cluster that hold the pack output at a steady 800 V whatever the state of charge, can spare weaker cells and replace the separate on-board charger; no launch date given
so: Pack electronics that fix the output voltage could free pack designers from series cell counts and drop the on-board charger; still in development.

headline: Two sodium-ion material projects are signed in Neijiang, Sichuan: Jiangxi Jinhui plans 30,000 t a year of sodium hexafluorophosphate and 100,000 t of sodium-ion electrolyte, and Yonghan Materials a battery-grade NFPP cathode line
so: China keeps building a sodium-ion materials supply chain: a sign that sodium-ion cells for storage and small EVs are heading to volume.

headline: India's Cabinet approves a ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh of grid-scale storage between FY27 and FY31 (30 GWh of battery storage, 60 GWh pumped hydro, 2 GWh other technologies), allocated by tariff-based bidding, with at least 40% domestic content required for battery projects
short: India backs 30 GWh of battery storage with new VGF; 40% local content
so: New central funding for 30 GWh of battery storage to 2031, but with 40% local content: more demand, with pressure to source systems in India.

headline: NTPC Green Energy plans an international tender to buy 10 GW / 40 GWh of LFP battery containers and grid-forming power conversion systems for its projects, with supervision of installation and a 15-year service agreement; the bid documents are to follow on NTPC's portal
short: NTPC Green to tender 40 GWh of battery containers and grid-forming PCS
so: A single 40 GWh equipment buy, open to foreign suppliers: one of the largest storage procurements yet and a strong pull on container suppliers.

headline: India's Cabinet also approves a ₹2,814 crore capital-subsidy scheme for domestic processing of lithium, nickel and other critical minerals, covering two lithium and two nickel processing plants
so: Subsidies for two lithium and two nickel refineries in India: a first step toward local cell materials, years from output.

headline: Huawei Digital Power tells customers it will raise prices: 5–15% for inverters and residential and commercial storage, 5–10% for grid-forming utility storage and PCS, citing costlier commodities, circuit boards and memory; Sungrow, Growatt, Kehua and others raised prices earlier
so: Chinese PCS and storage equipment makers are raising prices 5–15%: non-cell parts of BESS quotes are getting dearer even as cells soften.

headline: Tata Motors' passenger EV chief Shailesh Chandra says Indian cell making should start within a year and cells and their materials could be localised in two to three years; Agratas' 20 GWh Sanand plant is due to start in 2027
so: An Indian carmaker expects local EV cells within a year and local materials in two to three: imported cells stay the norm until then.

headline: InfoLink, 4 Nov: China lithium carbonate falls 7.2% in a week to about $13,430 a tonne, spodumene 10% to $1,215; the 314 Ah storage cell eases 0.7% to $46.6/kWh and 2-hour DC containers 1%
so: Lithium down another 7% in a week while storage cells slip under 1%: cell prices are lagging the fall in raw materials.

headline: Dongfeng's Voyah, M-hero and Epicland brands are expected to be first with CATL's third-generation Shenxing LFP battery (10–80% in under 4 minutes, 10C or more) after a group-level deal on 29 Oct, a Chinese report says
so: 10C fast-charge LFP cells are heading into more Chinese cars: raises the bar for charging speed in EV cell specifications.

headline: CATL, Octopus Energy and Ampace (the ATL–CATL joint venture) sign an MoU on home storage in Europe, starting in the UK, France and Spain; Ampace will make the cells, BMS and storage units
so: China's largest cell maker moves into European home storage with a utility partner: more competition for residential battery makers.

headline: Citi cuts its three-month lithium carbonate target to $12,000 a tonne (from $20,000), hydroxide to $12,000 and spodumene to $1,200, and lowers estimates through 2028 on weaker 2027 battery demand and new supply such as a possible restart of CATL's Jianxiawo mine
so: A major bank now sees lithium staying cheap into 2028: supports lower cell prices in 2027 contracts.

headline: Rio Tinto adds 25,000 t a year of lithium carbonate capacity in Argentina for about $1.4 billion: the Fénix 1B expansion (+10,000 t, taking the site to about 40,000 t) and the new 15,000 t Sal de Vida operation, both producing since the second quarter
so: More lithium supply outside China from 2026–27: keeps raw-material costs down and widens sourcing options.

headline: LG Energy Solution guides fourth-quarter revenue about 10% higher with storage shipments up some 40%, says most of its North American storage output through 2028 is sold, plans more than 50 GWh of storage capacity there by end-2026 and 70 GWh by end-2027, and will cut capex by over 40%
so: Korean makers' US storage lines are sold out to 2028: little spare non-Chinese storage-cell supply in the near term.

headline: Chinese storage and battery Q3 results split: Gotion's revenue rose about 75% but it swung to a net loss, Sungrow's profit fell about 68% on revenue down 22%, while BYD (+28%), Deye (+89%) and HyperStrong (+71%) grew profits
so: Chinese storage makers are fighting on price and some are losing money: buyers keep bargaining power on cells and systems.

headline: Noida Power Company tenders an 80 MW / 320 MWh four-hour standalone battery in Greater Noida on a 12-year build-own-operate-transfer basis (bids of 20–80 MW, 95% monthly availability, e-reverse auction); bids are due 9 Dec
so: Another four-hour storage tender in Uttar Pradesh: small (320 MWh) but adds to Indian demand; bids due 9 Dec.

headline: Amara Raja's Q2 profit falls about 45% on revenue up 18.5%; its cell unit gets ₹2,320 crore of new capex over 30 months to lift pack capacity from 4 to 9 GWh and build an LFP cell plant in Telangana
so: Amara Raja is building an LFP cell plant and more pack capacity: another future Indian cell source.

headline: Energy In Motion and Sorigin Green Mobility agree to deploy 500 electric heavy trucks (EIM's 55-tonne Ashwa tractors) over two years on freight corridors, starting with 18 at JNPA port with battery swapping and pay-per-freight pricing
short: EIM and Sorigin plan 500 electric heavy trucks over two years
so: 500 battery-swap heavy e-trucks on Indian freight corridors: a large test of swapping against plug-in charging for heavy trucks.

headline: Webasto is in advanced talks with two strategic buyers to sell its battery-systems business, which makes high-voltage packs (anchor customer Hyundai-Kia) in Germany and Korea and had about €300 million of 2025 revenue, as it cuts group debt
so: A European pack maker is up for sale: consolidation among pack makers abroad.

headline: India's e-scooter makers step up capacity: TVS and Bajaj aim for about 80,000 EVs a month each by early 2027, Hero's VIDA targets over 80,000 a month by late 2027 and Ather is spending ₹122 crore to add 2.25 lakh units a year
so: Two-wheeler makers are adding big EV volumes: more demand for Indian-made cells, which may tighten local supply.

headline: Gujarat's regulator adopts the tariffs from GUVNL's Phase IX 450 MW / 900 MWh standalone storage auction: NLC India Renewables (275 MW) and Sun Drops Energia (175 MW) at about ₹2.32 lakh per MW per month, with VGF from the PSDF
so: Gujarat confirms storage tariffs near ₹2.32 lakh/MW/month: a benchmark for what Indian storage projects earn.

headline: India's electric car registrations jumped about 75% on a year in October to some 36,600 (JATO), lifting EV share of car sales to 7.3% while the overall car market shrank; Tata Motors (14,560) and Mahindra (8,473) lead
so: Electric cars gain share in India: more local battery demand helps Indian cell plants reach scale.

headline: China October EV sales: BYD sold 483,125 passenger cars, Geely 214,996 and Leapmotor 106,127 (up 51% on a year), while Huawei's HIMA brands fell by half and Li Auto slipped 9%
so: Strong China EV sales keep LFP cell demand high there, supporting cell prices.

headline: Sunwoda's EV battery unit says its 400 Wh/kg polymer-composite solid-state cell has passed design checks and is with customers for evaluation, with a 0.2 GWh pilot line running; CATL repeats its aim of small-batch solid-state output in 2027
so: Solid-state cells are still at pilot stage: no change for buses, trucks or storage in the next three years.

headline: SNE Research: global EV battery installations reached 994.5 GWh in January–September, up 19.7%; CATL holds 39.1% and BYD 15.2%, with LGES third at 8.2% and Gotion and CALB about 5% each
so: CATL and BYD hold over half of the world's EV cells: supply stays concentrated in two Chinese makers.

headline: Lithium carbonate futures bounce 2.5% to about $13,540 a tonne on 2 Nov while China spot holds near $13,960; SMM says more ore is arriving, smelter stocks are building and buyers are waiting, so it expects prices to stay near the lows
so: Lithium bounced but sellers expect prices to drift: no change to the near-term cell cost picture.

headline: NTPC's trading arm NVVN declares its first 250 MW / 500 MWh battery storage project commercial from 27 Oct, with power scheduling starting the next day; it is NTPC's first standalone BESS in operation
so: NTPC's first standalone storage project is running: proves the model and supports more central tenders.

headline: India's electric two-wheeler sales hit a record 2.23 lakh in October (Vahan), up 48% on a year: TVS leads with 60,429 (27%), then Bajaj 49,067, Ather 31,796 and Hero Vida 29,901, while Ola falls 26% to 12,096
so: Record e-scooter sales in India: more local cell demand, helping Indian cell plants scale.

headline: Jaipur discom JVVNL and the Global Energy Alliance seek bids for India's first sodium-ion battery storage pilot, a 250 kW / 250 kWh unit at a Jaipur stadium to be compared side by side with lithium-ion
so: India's first sodium-ion storage pilot: a small trial of an alternative chemistry for storage.

headline: Hina Battery plans a 10 GWh sodium-ion plant in Wuhan (first 3 GWh phase to start building in early 2027) and sodium-ion refuse trucks; sodium-ion and solid-state cells stay exempt from China's new battery consumption tax to end-2028, while lithium-ion pays 2% (4% from Sept 2027)
so: Sodium-ion is being built at scale for heavy vehicles in China: a possible cheaper chemistry later this decade.

headline: SMM: Q3 profits at Chinese lithium producers that buy ore collapsed (Ganfeng −68%, Tianqi −43% on the quarter, Sichuan New Energy into loss) while miners with their own low-cost resources held up; CATL's gross margin slipped to 20.7%
so: Lithium processors are losing money at today's prices: prices are near the floor, so the next big move is more likely up.

headline: Bloomberg: Hungary's post-Orbán political shake-up is hitting its EV battery industry (headline only, not verified)
so: Political change in Hungary may slow Europe's battery plants (headline only).

headline: BW ESS raises bank debt for its 400 MW / 1.4 GWh Hams Hall battery in England (first 350 MW phase due online before end-2026) and enters France by buying two 100 MW / 400 MWh projects from Recurrent Energy
so: Storage keeps growing in Europe: competes with India for the same Chinese storage cells.

headline: Jakson Green E-Mobility wins a PM-eBus Sewa tender for 220 nine-metre AC electric buses in Vadodara, Gandhidham and Navsari (Gujarat) on a 12-year gross-cost contract, including the charging depots
short: Jakson Green wins 220 electric buses for three Gujarat cities
so: 220 e-buses won in Gujarat under PM e-Bus Sewa: these gross-cost tenders drive India's e-bus market.

headline: Mecpower Solutions and Navitas Solar plan a 5 GWh BESS assembly and integration plant at Karjan, Gujarat (packs, racks, BMS, PCS, EMS), due to start in Q1 FY2027–28; cells will be bought in at first
so: A new 5 GWh storage-system assembly plant in Gujarat from 2027: more Indian capacity, buying cells from abroad at first.

headline: Samsung SDI's Q3 operating profit hits a 12-quarter high (about $285 million, revenue up 53%); it has booked over 60 GWh of storage-battery orders this year, filling its US and Ulsan lines to 2028, started prismatic LFP storage cells in Indiana and won its first European EV LFP order
so: Korean storage lines are booked to 2028: few non-Chinese storage cells free for Indian buyers soon.

headline: Lithium carbonate futures slump 8.4% in a day to about $13,190 a tonne on 29 Oct, and China spot drops 3.9% to about $14,340 after peaking the day before; SMM sees next week's range at roughly $11,940–$15,670 as stock drawdowns slow
so: Lithium fell 8% in a day: if it lasts, cell prices drift lower over the next few months.

headline: Pace Digitek wins Coal India's 187.5 MW / 750 MWh standalone battery project at Choutuppal, Telangana (₹1,074 crore, ₹3.14 lakh per MW a month, 11 bidders) and gets a BSES Rajdhani letter of intent for 57.5 MW / 115 MWh across four Delhi substations
so: ₹3.14 lakh/MW/month in a Coal India storage tender: a higher-than-usual tariff and a benchmark for Indian bids.

headline: Olectra's MD calls electric trucks a bigger opportunity than buses: its first trucks cover 28–55 tonne tippers and tractor-trailers, the Sitarampur plant is sized for about 1,200 trucks a year, and he says about 74% of state bus purchases in Q1 were electric
so: Olectra moves into electric heavy trucks (tippers and tractor-trailers): more makers in India's e-truck market.

headline: Tamil Nadu's regulator (TNERC) clears the state discom to buy 600 MW of solar plus 300 MW / 1.8 GWh of six-hour storage from SECI's ISTS Tranche XXI at ₹3.12/kWh for 25 years; storage must supply evening and night peaks (6 pm–9 am)
short: Tamil Nadu clears 600 MW solar with 1.8 GWh storage at ₹3.12/kWh
so: Tamil Nadu buys solar plus six-hour storage: more storage demand in the state.

headline: Chinese storage maker Sigenergy plans a $150–200 million battery and inverter factory in India, shortlisting Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu; it would start with imported cells and needs government approval as a Chinese investor (report citing the Times of India)
so: A Chinese storage maker plans an Indian factory: more competition in Indian storage systems.

headline: Blue Energy Motors and HPCL open a heavy e-truck battery-swap station at an HPCL outlet in Bhiwandi on the Mumbai–Pune electric freight corridor; a swap takes under five minutes
so: Battery swapping for heavy e-trucks opens on the Mumbai–Pune corridor: swap infrastructure for freight is arriving.

headline: Paradeep Parivahan signs a 10-year deal with JSW Cement and JSW Eco-Mobility to run 100 electric heavy trucks hauling about 125,000 t of clinker and slag a month from Nandyal (Andhra Pradesh) to Vijayanagar (Karnataka)
so: 100 electric heavy trucks on a 10-year industrial haul contract: long fleet deals are making e-trucks bankable.

headline: EVE Energy tells investors its fourth-quarter cell capacity is fully booked and output will rise on the quarter; inventory turnover is about 56 days and it will run leaner stock while raw-material prices swing
so: EVE's cell capacity is fully booked: supply is tight at big makers, limiting discounts in near-term quotes.

headline: Haryana Power Purchase Centre (the state's two discoms) invites bids for solar projects with battery storage inside Haryana; bids are due 17 November (capacity not stated in the report)
so: Haryana tenders solar with storage: more Indian storage demand; bids due 17 Nov.

headline: Business Today: India is planning a ₹12,000-crore PLI for cell materials (cathode and anode active materials, electrolyte, separators, foil); under the existing ₹18,100-crore ACC PLI only Ola runs cell capacity (2.5 of its 20 GWh) and no maker has yet been paid an incentive, while cell imports keep climbing
short: India plans a ₹12,000-crore PLI for cell materials
so: A proposed incentive for cell materials in India: would make local cell-making cheaper and less dependent on China.

headline: Australia's resources department forecasts spodumene averaging about US$2,499/t in FY2027, up 63% from about US$1,532/t in FY2026, before easing to about US$1,684/t by FY2031
so: Australia expects spodumene prices to rise sharply in 2027: a risk that lithium and cell costs climb again.

headline: CATL Europe's Akin Li: its standard swappable packs (#20, #25, #26 for cars, 75# for heavy trucks) fit about 85% of China's A-segment models; truck swaps take about 5 minutes vs about 25 at a charger, and its three European plants will exceed 150 GWh
so: CATL's standard swappable packs for heavy trucks: a model that could reach India's freight corridors.

headline: Adani Green switches on another 3.08 GWh of battery storage at Khavda in July–September, taking the site to about 6.6 GWh, which it says is more than half of India's operating BESS capacity
so: Adani is building storage at huge scale for its own solar: part of India's storage demand is served in-house, not tendered.

headline: BloombergNEF raises its 2026 forecast: global storage additions to jump 45% to about 188 GW / 535 GWh (from 158 GW / 459 GWh expected in mid-year), with India adding more than 6 GW this year and 638 GWh worldwide in 2027
so: BloombergNEF raises its storage forecast, with India adding over 6 GW this year: a bigger market.

headline: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence expects lithium demand from stationary storage to slow from more than 60% a year to about 5% a year through 2030; total lithium demand seen rising from 2.1 million t LCE in 2026 to about 7 million t by 2050
so: Lithium demand from storage expected to slow: supports lower lithium and cell prices later this decade.

headline: ACME Solar signs an FDRE (firm, dispatchable renewables) power deal with SECI for 300 MW of solar with 1.2 GWh of co-located batteries (4 hours of supply after sunset) at about $0.063/kWh
short: ACME wins SECI deal: 300 MW solar with 1.2 GWh of batteries
so: A large solar-plus-storage power deal in India: more demand for storage.

headline: Mercom: India's battery-storage manufacturing capacity reaches about 86 GWh, but 92% is pack/container assembly and only 8% is cell making; most capacity is still under construction, mainly in Gujarat and Maharashtra
so: India has lots of pack and container assembly but little cell-making: storage still depends on imported cells.

headline: Gujarat's power regulator (GERC) notifies its first grid-interactive battery-storage regulations, covering planning, procurement, operation and scheduling of BESS; standalone storage may not serve captive or third-party renewable plants
so: Gujarat sets rules for grid batteries: clearer rules make storage projects easier to finance and tender.

headline: India's transmission utility CTUIL sets a minimum storage duration for BESS grid-connectivity applications: four hours for specified applications, two hours for eligible right-of-first-refusal cases
so: Four-hour minimum storage for grid connections: more battery energy per project.

headline: Switch Mobility delivers the first six of 50 EiV12 electric intercity coaches to Pune-based Purple Bus for the Nagpur–Chandrapur route (claimed range up to 350 km)
so: First electric intercity coaches delivered for the Nagpur–Chandrapur route: e-buses are moving beyond city service.

headline: CATL shares drop more than 10% after Q3: profit up 14.5% but margin slips to 20.7% as China's new 2% battery consumption tax and the end of export VAT rebates (1 Jan 2027) bite; JPMorgan downgrades the Hong Kong shares
so: China's new battery tax and the end of export rebates on 1 Jan 2027 raise the cost of Chinese cells for importers by several percent.

headline: Lopal unit signs a 2026–2030 deal to supply about 379,000–568,000 t of LFP cathode; SMM puts mid-October NEV-grade LFP at about $7,090/t, roughly 60% above the June 2025 low
so: Long cathode supply deals in China: cathode makers locking in demand.

headline: Tata Power's strategy head says Indian standalone BESS tariffs have fallen more than 80% since 2022, against about 40% for packs; analysts see up to three-quarters of awarded 2-hour capacity at risk
so: Indian storage tariffs have fallen over 80% since 2022 and many awarded projects may not be built: a growing market on very thin prices.

headline: China lithium spot edges down to about $15,280/t as buyers wait for lower prices
so: Lithium edging down: no change yet.

headline: CATL launches a swappable 'dual-electric' battery system for heavy trucks (432–513 kWh main pack plus 77 kWh backup) and targets 900 swap stations by end-2026
so: CATL's swappable heavy-truck batteries: a model for e-truck freight that could reach India.

headline: CATL's third-quarter profit misses estimates as competition and outlook concerns weigh (headline only, not verified)
so: CATL's profit miss (headline only): competition among cell makers stays strong.

headline: Vikram Solar unit VSL PowerHive plans a 7.5 GWh/yr BESS assembly plant near Chennai (scalable to 15 GWh), operating from April 2027, with 7.5 GWh of cell making planned from 2028
so: A 7.5 GWh storage plant near Chennai from 2027, with cell-making from 2028: more local capacity, and a possible local cell source.

headline: MAHAGENCO tenders 500 MW / 1.6 GWh of battery storage, build-own-operate; bids due 5 Nov
so: Maharashtra tenders 1.6 GWh of storage: more demand; bids due 5 Nov.

headline: Varroc to buy 45% of Forsee Power India and take control, starting with battery packs for electric three-wheelers; Energy In Motion opens a 5,000-a-year electric heavy-truck plant with pack lines in Pune
so: Energy In Motion opens a 5,000-a-year electric heavy-truck plant: new capacity in India's e-truck market.

headline: CNNC awards a 2.98 GWh storage framework at about $66–70/kWh; Sungrow and CATL among five winners
so: A big Chinese storage award at $66–70/kWh: confirms low system prices, a benchmark for imported systems.

headline: China September storage awards: 4-hour systems down 12% to about $70/kWh
so: Chinese 4-hour storage awards fell 12% in a month to about $70/kWh: imported system costs keep falling.

headline: Gotion begins commissioning its LFP cell plant in Kenitra, Morocco (first phase about $1.3 billion, up to 20 GWh a year planned) to supply Africa, Europe, the Middle East and the US
so: Gotion's LFP cell plant in Morocco: a non-China source of LFP cells for the future.

headline: China's September EV battery installations reach 87.2 GWh, 85.5% LFP; CATL 40.9%, BYD 21.1%, CALB 7.0% share
so: LFP is 85% of China's EV cells and CATL holds 41%: supply stays concentrated.

headline: Bloomberg: lithium extends its slump as battery demand worries mount; down about 14% on the week
so: Lithium slumped 14% in a week (headline only): cell costs easing.

headline: CRISIL expects electric buses to reach about 17% of new bus registrations in India next fiscal year, up from 7% in FY26; public orders total about 29,000 e-buses
so: CRISIL expects electric buses to reach 17% of new bus sales in India next year: a fast-growing market.

headline: China will cut the export VAT rebate on EVs, e-buses and electric truck tractors from 13% to 9% from 1 April 2027; the separate battery export rebate (now 6%) is still due to end on 1 January 2027
so: China cuts its export rebate on e-buses and e-truck tractors from April 2027: Chinese e-buses and e-trucks get dearer abroad.

headline: Tata Motors (commercial vehicles) Q2: wholesale volumes up 42% to about 135,100, revenue up 36% and back in profit; exports up 177%. Its Iveco takeover offer closes 26 Oct, with settlement planned for 30 Oct
so: Tata Motors' truck volumes up 42% and profitable again: India's truck market is strong.

headline: Andhra Pradesh (APPCC) tenders 1,250 MW / 5 GWh of standalone battery storage at three sites, build-own-operate; bids due 23 Nov
short: Andhra Pradesh tenders 5 GWh of standalone battery storage
so: Andhra Pradesh tenders 5 GWh of storage: a large new market; bids due 23 Nov.

headline: Telangana (TGREDCO) tenders 3 GW of solar with 1 GW / 6 GWh of energy storage, bids due 4 Nov; TGGENCO's 187.5 MW / 750 MWh Maheswaram storage tender closed 19 Oct
short: Telangana tenders 3 GW of solar with 6 GWh of storage
so: Telangana tenders 6 GWh of storage with solar: a large new market.

headline: NTPC Green tenders a turnkey EPC contract for 3.3 GWh of battery storage at its Khavda solar park in Gujarat (three 300 MW/900 MWh blocks and one 200 MW/600 MWh), with 15 years of O&M
short: NTPC Green tenders 3.3 GWh of battery storage at Khavda
so: NTPC tenders a 3.3 GWh turnkey storage build: a large contract for storage suppliers and EPC firms.

headline: GreenCell Mobility raises equity from Impact Fund Denmark to grow its electric bus fleet to more than 5,000 buses across 105 Indian cities (about 4,500 now being rolled out)
so: An e-bus operator raises money for over 5,000 buses: more demand for electric buses.

headline: China's storage chain recovers: EVE Energy forecasts nine-month profit up 80–90% on revenue up about 60%; Ganfeng Lithium's nine-month revenue rises 147%; inverter maker Deye's profit rises about 80%
so: China's storage chain is profitable again: cell makers have less need to cut prices.

headline: CATL and SERES (AITO) sign a long-term deal: a second Chongqing plant phase adds 10–12 GWh a year (over 20 GWh in total), and they will go after Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia together
so: CATL deepens ties with a carmaker: long supply deals keep its capacity committed.

headline: EnergyX and Trafigura sign a 10-year take-or-pay offtake for 100,000 t of battery-grade lithium from Chile (carbonate) and Texas (hydroxide), worth over $2 billion at about $20,000/t
so: A long lithium supply deal from Chile and Texas: more non-China lithium for the market.

headline: CATL launches Tener+, a 9 MWh grid storage system it says needs up to 40% fewer containers, at All Energy Australia; it also brings its Tener Sodium system (over 30 MWh, rated to 55°C) to Australia and signs MoUs with Hitachi Energy and EPEC
so: CATL's larger storage containers cut site costs: pushes system prices and site costs down.

headline: Amazon will put 3,000 Tata Motors electric trucks on Indian roads, starting with Ultra E.7 light trucks (96 kWh LFP pack, about 130 km range) in Delhi; the first 20 were flagged off and the Delhi–Chennai NH48 corridor comes next
short: Amazon to run 3,000 Tata electric trucks in India
so: Amazon's 3,000 Tata electric trucks: large fleets in India are switching to electric light trucks.

headline: SMM expects a lithium supply surge in 2026–28 (about 458,000 t of new primary resource this year and about 500,000 t in each of 2027 and 2028) after the 2022–23 spending wave; it sees storage demand up as much as 64% this year but says price rebounds will be uneven
so: A lithium supply surge expected through 2028: supports lower cell costs over the next three years.

headline: SECI tenders 4 GW / 16 GWh of standalone four-hour battery storage on a build-own-operate basis (10 GWh in Rajasthan, 6 GWh in Gujarat) with central support of ₹15 lakh per MWh (about ₹2,400 crore), a 20-year PPA and at least 51% renewable charging
short: SECI tenders 16 GWh of standalone battery storage in Rajasthan, Gujarat
so: 16 GWh of four-hour storage with central support: one of India's largest storage tenders, for delivery from 2027–28.

headline: Tamil Nadu's BESS Policy 2026 targets at least 2.5 GW / 10 GWh: new solar and hybrid plants of 1 MW and up must add four-hour storage equal to 10% of capacity, the state discom will buy 10 GWh in a first phase, and storage gets a ten-year transmission and wheeling charge waiver
short: Tamil Nadu mandates 4-hour storage on new solar; plans 10 GWh buy
so: Tamil Nadu makes new solar plants add four-hour storage and plans to buy 10 GWh: a large new state market.

headline: Waaree Renewable Technologies wins a letter of award from an unnamed Indian power producer to build a 200 MW / 500 MWh battery storage project (EPC), due for completion in FY2027-28; the value was not disclosed
so: A solar EPC firm wins another storage build: Indian EPC players are moving into storage.

headline: Hero MotoCorp has doubled its VIDA e-scooter capacity to 30,000 a month and plans 45,000 by Q4 FY27 and over 80,000 by Q2 FY28, saying the market is capacity-constrained; Bajaj, TVS and Ather are also expanding as India's e-two-wheeler registrations rose about 89% on a year in September
so: Two-wheeler makers are expanding fast: more demand for Indian cells.

headline: Xiaomi plans to invest about $253 million for a 5.34% stake in Sunwoda's EV battery unit, following Li Auto; Sunwoda will stop consolidating the unit and drops its Hong Kong listing plan
so: Carmakers are buying into cell makers to secure supply: long-term cell access is at a premium.

headline: GAC's battery arm Inpow starts its first overseas pack plant in Chonburi, Thailand (first pack off the line on 29 Oct; about $1.6 billion total investment), and plans storage work with Thai utility EGAT
so: Chinese battery makers are building packs abroad: a pattern that could reach India as they localise.

headline: Group14 picks Sagunt, Spain, for a 10 GWh plant making its SCC55 silicon-carbon anode material (a graphite replacement), backed by a new €150 million investment; its planned capacity would reach 40 GWh
so: A new anode material plant in Europe: long-term technology news, no near-term cost effect.

headline: Lithium carbonate futures in Guangzhou steady at about $13,210 a tonne on 30 Oct after the previous day's 8.4% slump, while the China spot benchmark falls another 2.6% to about $13,970
so: Lithium holding near $13,000–14,000: cell costs stay low for current quotes.
